detail:
MedlinePlus describes sleep apnea as a common disorder in which breathing stops or becomes very shallow during sleep, with pauses that can last from a few seconds to minutes and may occur 30 times or more an hour. The most common type is obstructive sleep apnea, in which the airway collapses or becomes blocked during sleep. In central sleep apnea, breathing pauses occur because the brain temporarily stops sending the signals that control breathing, and the two types can occur in the same person.

Symptoms can include loud snoring, pauses in breathing during sleep, daytime sleepiness, and morning headaches, and MedlinePlus notes that people with sleep apnea are at higher risk for car crashes, work-related accidents, and other medical problems. Clinicians usually diagnose sleep apnea from medical and family history, a physical exam, and the results of a sleep study, which can be done at home or in a sleep laboratory.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about sleep apnea symptoms and sleep studies.
summary: MedlinePlus describes sleep apnea as repeated pauses or shallow breathing during sleep, most often obstructive, in which the airway blocks, and sometimes central, in which the brain's breathing signals pause, diagnosed mainly with a sleep study.
takeaways: obstructive apnea involves a blocked or collapsed airway
central apnea involves paused brain signals for breathing
diagnosis usually rests on history, exam, and a sleep study
title: Sleep apnea: when breathing stops and restarts during sleep
